text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Latvian speaker Alfred Chepanis met with Russian counterpart Gennady Seleznov. Chepanis announced that for the time being relations between the two countries are frozen. He sees the visit as an attempt to start solving three major issues including the border and non-citizens.
- Talks between Chepanis and the first deputy speaker of the Russian Duma, Alexander Shokhin, focused on economic co-operation between Latvia and Russia.
- The Bank of Latvia agreed to a merger between Latvian Savings Bank and the Union Baltic Bank in Riga. The merger is due to happen in two months.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele held the first cabinet meeting of his new government, opened by President Guntis Ulmanis.
- Parliament passed the law on a free economic zone in the western port of Liepaja, Latvia's third largest port. The zone would give big tax breaks to companies which set up there.

- Russia's new ambassador, Alexander Udaltsov, held his first official press conference. He said that in July Latvia is likely to be visited by Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin in September.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas says the Vilnius-based correspondent of Diena misrepresents Lithuania to the Latvian public.

- Latvian ports handled 44.8 million tonnes of cargos in 1996. Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans believes that total cargo turnover will reach 50 million tonnes, including 3 million tons in Liepaja and 10 million tonnes in Riga.
